Playground Playbook
Internal platform playbook · Playground side

Build a module. Bundle a course. Ship a path.

How the platform turns single flows into courses, and courses into learning paths.

4 parts, then the demo 39 annotated screens Hover a number to reveal its label Enlarge a screenshot to see all labels at once

How the three pieces fit

Each one is made out of the one before it.

01
Part 01 · The building block

Individual Playground

An individual playground is one module. You build the flow on a canvas out of three node kinds, hang media and questions off each node, then release it so master playgrounds can pick it up.

Think of it as
A single module
Lives under
Courses, Playgrounds, All Playgrounds
Built from
Start node, custom nodes, end node
Released by
Save as Active

Order matters

A master playground can only attach playgrounds that already exist and are released. Always build the modules first, then bundle.

03

Find or start a flow

  1. Search or filter the existing flows before you create anything, so you do not duplicate a module that already exists.
  2. Press Create Interactive Flow to start a new module.
  3. Use the card icons to edit, duplicate or preview an existing flow. Duplicating is the fastest way to build a near copy.
  4. Note the Flow ID on each card. That is the value you will paste when anyone asks which module you mean.
Duplicate rather than rebuild

The copy arrives named Copy_ plus the original name. Rename it immediately so the list stays readable.

Name the playground

  2. Write the Description. It shows on the list card and inside master playgrounds.
The User-facing tag is a warning

Any field carrying the User-facing tag is read by learners. Do not park internal notes, ticket numbers or test strings in those fields.

05

Set time and objective

Create Playground, second half
Create Playground, second half Hover a number to read its label

  1. Enter Estimated Time to Complete in minutes. Learners see this number and master playgrounds add it up.
  2. Write the Objective. Only markdown is supported, so inline HTML and styling belong in a styled block if you need visual structure.
  3. Switch to Preview before saving to check the objective renders the way you expect.
  4. Press Create Playground.
Creating is only step one

Create Playground makes an empty shell with a Start and an End node. The actual content is built afterwards on the canvas.

Linked Masters is your blast radius

Before you change a module, read Linked Masters. Every course listed there inherits your edit immediately.

Style the objective block

Consistency beats cleverness

Objectives that share one visual template make a course feel finished. Ad hoc styling per module is the fastest way to make it look broken.

09

Build the flow on the canvas

Playground builder
Playground builder Hover a number to read its label
Slot 09 · builder-basic
Flow builder with node library, canvas and configuration panel
Click to add this screenshot, or drop them all at once
11Start, content, end22Drag custom nodes from here33All configuration happens in this panel44Content Type: markdown, video, image, PDF or audio55No cycles must stay green66Draft while building, Active to release
  1. Read the canvas top to bottom. The Start node opens, custom nodes carry the content, the End node closes.
  2. Drag a Custom Node from the library for every piece of content or every question you need.
  3. Select a node, then configure it in the right panel. Nothing is configured on the canvas itself.
  4. Set Content Type on the node to match what it holds. Markdown for text, or video, image, PDF or audio for a single asset served from S3.
  5. Watch Flow Analytics. No cycles must stay green, otherwise learners can be trapped in a loop.
  6. Save as Draft while you work. Save as Active only when the module is finished.
Three node kinds, one job each

Start opens the module and cannot be removed. Custom carries every piece of content and every question. End closes the module and is what marks completion.

Every asset needs an S3 link first

Video, image, PDF and audio nodes all point at an S3 public URL. Part 03 is how you produce that link. Upload before you build the node, not after.

Build a flow that asks questions

Playground builder, question flow

11Explain first22One idea per question node33Is Answered gates the next step44Counts should match your plan55Question type for the selected node
  1. Lead with an explanation node so learners meet the concept before they are tested on it.
  2. Add one question node per idea. Do not stack several questions onto a single node.
  3. Notice the edges read Is Answered. A question node will not release the learner until it is answered.
  4. Confirm the node and edge counts in Flow Analytics match what you intended to build.

Pick the question type

Configuration panel, Question Type

Question Type dropdown with three options
Click to add this screenshot, or drop them all at once
11One correct answer22Several correct answers33Free text, needs manual review
  1. Use Single Choice when exactly one option is correct. This is the default and the safest.
  2. Use Multiple Choice when more than one option is correct.
  3. Use Subjective for free text. Nothing is auto scored, so a human has to review it.
Subjective changes the workload

Every subjective question you add is future manual review effort. Use it only where a choice question genuinely cannot capture the answer.

Metadata is not a comment field

Question Metadata is User-facing. It renders alongside the question, so it is for the scenario the learner needs, not for notes to yourself.

Common trap

Renaming an option label after you set the correct answer can silently break the pairing. Always reselect the correct answer after any label edit.

Wire the node behaviour and its exit

Configuration panel, Node Configuration

  1. Set the Node Sequence ID.

  5. Save as Active only when every node in the flow has been configured.
Draft and Active

Save as Draft keeps your work private and leaves the live version untouched. Save as Active publishes it, and any course already using this module picks up the change.

Part 02 · The course

Master Playground

A master playground is the course. It carries no content of its own. Its whole job is to take individual playgrounds and put them in a deliberate order, with one set of instructions across the top.

Think of it as
A course

What a good instruction block says

How many modules there are, that they run in sequence, that all videos and materials should be viewed, and that knowledge checks should be attempted. Learners drop off when none of that is stated.

Sequence is the design

A course is only as good as its order. Put context and welcome material first, concept modules next, and the hands on task last.

03
Part 03 · The prerequisite

Video and media to S3 link

Playground nodes do not hold files. They hold links. Before you can build a video, image, audio or PDF node, the asset has to be pushed to the S3 bucket and turned into a public URL.

Lives under
Utility, Upload File
Video only goes to
Miscellaneous
Assets used in markdown go to
Public Resources
Max file size
500 MB

The four step procedure

  1. Open Utility, then Upload File.
  2. Select Location. Use Public Resources for anything referenced from markdown, and Miscellaneous for a video on its own.
  3. Rename the file so it has no spaces between words, then Browse and upload.
  4. Wait for the batch to appear in Upload History, then press Re-Generate Public URL to get the sheet of public links.

Open Utility

Utility
Utility Hover a number to read its label
Slot 25 · utility-landing
Utility landing with Upload File and File Upload History
Click to add this screenshot, or drop them all at once
11Utility in the menu22Push a new asset33Get links for an old one
  1. Open Utility from the left menu.
  2. Choose Upload File to push a new asset.
  3. Choose File Upload History to fetch links for something already uploaded.
26

Select the location, then upload

Utility, Upload File
Utility, Upload File Hover a number to read its label
Slot 26 · file-uploader
File Uploader with the Select Location dropdown open
Click to add this screenshot, or drop them all at once
11Supported types only22Choose destination first33Markdown assets go here44Standalone video goes here55No spaces in file names
  1. Check the supported file types before you start, since anything else will be rejected.
  2. Open Select Location. Nothing can be uploaded until a destination is chosen.
  3. Pick Public Resources for assets that will be referenced from markdown content.
  4. Pick Miscellaneous when you are uploading a video on its own.
  5. Rename the file first so there are no spaces between words, then Browse and upload. Keep each file under 500 MB.
Why the file name matters

Spaces in a file name break the resulting URL in ways that are painful to trace. Use underscores, for example Fine_Tuning.mp4.

Two destinations mean two sheets

Miscellaneous and Public Resources produce separate sheets of links. Keep track of which destination you used, or you will hunt for a link in the wrong sheet.

27

Generate the public URL

Utility, Upload History
Utility, Upload History Hover a number to read its label
Slot 27 · upload-history
Upload History batch with Private URI and Re-Generate Public URL
Click to add this screenshot, or drop them all at once
11Your batch, tagged by destination22Must read Success33Private URI will not work in a node44This produces the CSV of public links
  1. Find your batch. Each upload becomes a numbered batch tagged with its destination.
  2. Confirm Status reads Success. If it does not, the Reason column says why.
  3. Note that the Private URI shown is not usable in a playground node.
  4. Press Re-Generate Public URL. A CSV of public URIs is generated for that batch.
  5. Open the CSV, copy the public URL, and paste it into the media node you are building.
Do this before you build the node

Uploading and link generation is a prerequisite, not a cleanup step. Get the public URL in hand, then go and configure the media node.

04
Part 04 · The programme

Learning Path

A learning path is the full journey. It strings together master playgrounds, assessments, verification and tax steps as ordered workflow steps, and it attaches a campaign mail to each step so learners are told when to move.

Think of it as
A programme
Lives under
Courses, Learning Paths
Built from
Master playgrounds, assessments, verification steps
Per step
Entity, progression and campaign

Top to bottom is execution order

35

Configure one step: what it is and how learners advance

Workflow steps, Entity type
Workflow steps, Entity type Hover a number to read its label
Slot 35 · lp-step-config
Step with the Entity type list open
Click to add this screenshot, or drop them all at once
11Learner facing step name22Open Entity type33A master playground sits under Courses44Manual or automatic advance55Preview updates as you go
  1. Write the Step name. It is learner facing.
  2. Open Entity type to say what this step actually is.
  3. Pick from Courses, Assessments, AI Interviews, Live trainings, Task or Live Tasking. A master playground sits under Courses.
  4. Set Progression. Manual means someone has to qualify the learner before they advance. Automatic advances them on completion.
  5. Watch the Step flow preview fill in as you go.
Manual progression is a queue

Every step set to Manual creates review work for someone. Use it where a human judgement is genuinely required, and Automatic where completion is enough.

  2. Search the list and pick the mail that belongs to this stage of the journey.
  3. If the mail does not exist yet, use Create new campaign.

Campaign mails are per step

This is the part people miss. A learning path does not send one mail. Each step carries its own campaign, so the learner is prompted at the right moment for that stage.

11Confirm which step you are acting on22Apply filters to unlock bulk actions33Notify learners on this step44Qualifying may advance them55Verify the result
  1. Confirm Current Step in the top right is the step you mean to act on.
  2. Filter the list, then Apply filters. Bulk actions only unlock once rows are selected or filters applied.
  3. Select the campaign template and press Send campaign to notify those learners.
  4. Use Update qualification to set the outcome on this step. Qualifying a learner may advance them to the next step.
  5. Check the table to confirm status, qualification and progress moved as expected.
Two ways a mail goes out

The campaign attached to a step in the workflow builder covers the designed journey. Send campaign here is the manual nudge for learners who have stalled on a step.

When something looks broken

Six symptoms and what actually causes them.

!A module is missing from the master builder
Master Playgrounds is still off on that module, or its access type is still Under Validation.
!A media node shows nothing
The node is pointing at the private S3 URI instead of the public URL from the generated CSV.
!The correct answer will not select
An option label was renamed after the correct answer was set. Reselect it.
!A learner never advances past a step
That step is set to Manual progression and nobody has qualified them yet.
!Learners do not know a new stage opened
The step has no campaign attached, so no mail was ever sent.
!A link is broken for no clear reason
The uploaded file name had a space in it. Rename and re upload.
